title: Give a split window's space back to the window it came from
body:
## Problem
Closing, minimizing, floating ("undocking"), tab-merging, or dragging out a tiled window resizes every window in its row or column, so their terminals reflow. Wanted, in the user's words "simple and intuitive": if I split view A to make window B, then minimize, close or float B, A gets its space back and the layout looks like it did before the split. That should only happen if it still makes sense, meaning A is still right beside B. Otherwise today's behaviour is fine.

## Cause (from reading the code; not reproduced in the GUI)
- Every exit goes through `WindowManager::detach` (src/wm.rs), which calls `LayoutTree::remove` (src/layout.rs). `remove` rescales the whole split (`*r /= total`).
- Only one kind of insert loses information: the same-axis branch of `LayoutTree::insert_split`. It halves the target and adds B as a flat sibling, so [A .5, C .5] becomes [A .25, B .25, C .5]. Removing B rescales to [A .33, C .67]: C grows and A never gets back to .5. The other inserts (the nested branch, and `insert_root`) wrap A and B in a new two-child split, and `remove` already collapses that back exactly.
- Restore from 8716dc0 (`restore_slot` / `Reentry::insert_flat`) takes the share back proportionally, which is the exact inverse of today's proportional remove.
- Floating a window back in (`toggle_float_for`) ignores where the window came from. It splits whatever leaf is under the window's center, 50/50.

## Design: give the space back to the window it came from
1. `LayoutTree` records `split_from: HashMap<WinId, WinId>` (B -> A). Only the same-axis branch of `insert_split` writes it. It lives in memory only: a fresh tree (restart, layout Apply) starts empty, and those cases keep today's behaviour.
2. `remove(B)`: if one of B's direct neighbours in its split contains `split_from[B]`, add B's whole ratio to that neighbour and change no other ratio. Otherwise rescale as today. "Still matches" is about position (confirmed by the user 2026-10-21): a resized A, or an A that was split again, still counts. An A that is gone or no longer next to B does not. Don't restore A's old size, because that would undo resizes the user made after the split.
3. When a window X leaves and its share goes to R, every entry with `split_from` X now points at R, since R covers X's space. Drop X's own entry.
4. Restore is the exact inverse. `Reentry::insert_flat` takes the share back from that same neighbour when it sits beside the re-entry point; otherwise it takes it proportionally, as today.
5. Floating a window back in through `toggle_float_for` uses the same slot memory as unminimize (`min_slots`, recorded when the window floats out) instead of the center split. If that fails, use today's path.

Out of scope: a new layout model, any change to the "tiled iff leaf" rule, persisted state.

## Gotchas
- Never record the Sessions panel in `split_from`: `insert_beside_panel` splits the panel's own leaf. Otherwise a closed window would hand its share to the panel, and `repin_panel` would then shove it onto some other window.
- `drop_proposal` clones the tree for the preview. `commit_drop` re-runs the insert on the real tree when the mouse is released, so the map is written there. Never keep a clone's map.
- `ghost_tree` / `min_slots_of` replay remove and restore on clones. Remove and restore must stay exact inverses, or `unminimize_in_any_order_gives_back_the_layout` (src/wm.rs) fails. That test is the safety net, so keep it green.
- The desktop and Projects run the same engine, so a Project split from another Project gets the same behaviour.

## Acceptance
- layout.rs table tests for each lossy insert (flat H and flat V, 3+ siblings, next to the Sessions panel):
  - insert then remove gives back bit-identical ratios;
  - with A resized in between, remove changes only A;
  - with A gone or moved away, remove rescales exactly as today.
- wm.rs: minimizing, floating or closing a window split from A leaves every window except A at its old rect. Restoring it, or floating it back in, gives back the rects from before it left.
- Gate: `cargo test --target-dir target/agent` and clippy pass. GUI proof: ask the user to run build-screenshot.
- Docs: update the removal rule in docs/tiling-tree.md (note that restart and Apply clear the memory) and the minimize-restore section of docs/task-manager-panel.md.

## Noticed, separate card if wanted
After minimize then restore, the project-layout Modified flag stays on even when the arrangement is identical again. `watch_layout_edits` compares with the previous capture, not with the layout definition.
